description: We’re Berno and Sabito. It’s our first hackathon: we’re here to learn, think and create. We’ll build a mission design game where every choice affects mass, power and budget. We’re looking for someone with coding, design, art, space knowledge, presenting skills. No need to be an expert, just curious and eager to create together. Join us!
summary:
Mission Trade-Off is an interactive educational web game where 1–4 players design, build and simulate a complete space mission to Mars. Players select real spacecraft components (bus, propulsion, power, communications, instruments and crew health systems) while managing mass, power, budget, environmental impact and crew risk in real time.

After designing the spacecraft, players enter a simulation phase featuring realistic NASA-based events — including orbital debris conjunctions, solar flares, micrometeorite impacts, communication blackouts and crew fatigue — and must make decisions under pressure. The final mission report combines design quality with simulation performance and provides actionable recommendations.

Built with Next.js and deployed on Vercel, the game teaches the complex trade-offs of space mission design using real NASA data and operational scenarios, while emphasizing that space is humanity’s common heritage.
details:
Project Name

Mission Trade-Off

Short Summary

An interactive web game where 1-4 players design, build and simulate a complete space mission, balancing engineering, environmental impact and crew health in real time.

What it does

Imagine you have $350M, 1,200 kg and 1,000 W to map Mars. A better camera chokes your data link. A cheaper engine leaves more debris. Skimp on shielding and radiation builds up silently. Every choice helps one thing and costs another. Welcome to Mission Trade-Off.

Designing a space mission means constant trade-offs between science goals, engineering limits, cost, environmental impact and crew health. For students and the public, those trade-offs stay abstract. Mission Trade-Off makes them tangible, playable and educational.

Players pick a spacecraft bus, propulsion, instruments, communications and crew health systems for an MVP scenario: Mars high-resolution mapping (≤5 m/pixel over 70%+ of the planet). A live dashboard turns green, yellow or red across three axes: Engineering & Resources, Environmental Impact, and Crew Health & Risk. Then they simulate the mission, face random hazards such as debris, solar flares and micrometeorites, and get a scored report with recommendations.

How we built it

Next.js 16, React 19, Tailwind CSS 4, Zustand 5 and TypeScript, deployed on Vercel. The score weighs Scientific Value (35%), Resource Efficiency (20%), Mission Objectives (15%), Environmental Impact (15%) and Crew Health (15%). Berno, our lead developer, playtested the demo throughout the two days of the hackathon, fixing bugs and refining the gameplay after each round of testing.

Why it matters

It’s the only mission design game we know of that includes all three axes. It teaches systems thinking, responsible use of resources and debris awareness, and it puts crew health at the center of design. Space is humanity’s common heritage, and every mission leaves a mark.

What’s next

Real-time multiplayer, 3D spacecraft visualization, an educator mode with lesson plans, and more scenarios (Asteroid Defense, Lunar Base, Europa Clipper).
